note: Three short blocks take two first chords from clean shapes to changes on the bar line to strumming every beat, each over a metronome with the chord blocks lit, so the hands change task every few minutes and the timer matches each step.

exercise.title: Em to Am, clean and in time
exercise.focus: Em-Am changes · strumming with the metronome at 60 bpm
exercise.why: Em and Am share a finger shape, so they are the easiest first change to make automatic.

sections.text: Em and Am use the same two fingers side by side: learn to move them as one unit and the change becomes a single motion.

items: Fret Em as shown. Strum once and pick each string; every one should ring.
Fret Am as shown. Pick each string again.
Switch back and forth slowly, 10 times, moving the two fingers both shapes share together without lifting them far from the strings.

sections.text: Press Play: after one bar of count-in, strum down once on beat 1 of each bar, on the lit chord, and let it ring. Use beats 2 to 4 to get your fingers to the next chord before its bar starts. Done when every change lands on beat 1 for a whole minute.
Now strum down on every beat at 60 and change chords every bar: Em, Am, Em, Am. Done when you change without missing the first beat of a bar, four times in a row.
